name: Russell H. Taylor
title: John C. Malone Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science; secondary Mechanical Engineering and School of Medicine appointments
fitReason: Strong CS overlap in 3D scene understanding, language-guided robot planning and human-supervised physical execution, within a surgical-robotics research environment. The verified AI hardware study is collaborative; a direct project with Taylor and the appropriate day-to-day mentor would need to be identified.

physicalEvidence.summary: A full collaborative primary study integrates SAM2, FoundationPose and GPT-4o with an actual da Vinci Classic/dVRK and Azure Kinect for benchtop peg transfer and gauze retrieval. Closed-loop trials use human supervisory feedback, predefined robot actions and linear waypoint motion; they are not autonomous clinical surgery. The study first appeared September 19, 2024, was presented at COLAS 2025, and has a May 11, 2026 arXiv revision. Separately, the official 2026 REU project list names Taylor as PI and describes his lab’s already-developed endoscope-control arm; the proposed new safety prototype is not treated as a completed result. The particular learned dVRK experiment was not independently tied to a current Taylor advisee, so hardware credit is conservatively collaborative.

shortVisit.summary: The 2026 LCSR REU lists a Taylor-supervised vision/robot-safety project, but its current eligibility is undergraduate students who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. It does not establish external-master’s eligibility. The CIIS openings page was last modified in 2019 and describes degree admissions and undergraduate projects. No current external-master’s short-visit invitation was verified.
